partition_and_assignment: Sequential model segments are allocated across clusters, and spatial input ranges are divided within each cluster. Mapping of receptive fields and padding preserve dependencies. A separate compressor reduces intermediate traffic. [pp. 5–7, §§III–IV; p. 9, §VI, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The study distinguishes indoor airborne-computer measurements from its outdoor deployment on five UAVs. The results specify different configurations and video resolutions where appropriate. [pp. 10–12, Fig. 12, §VIII.A–B and Fig. 13, OBSERVED]

[pp. 7 and 10, §§IV.C and VII.B; p. 13, §VIII.C, Fig. 16(b) and Table IV, PARTIAL]

title: Efficient AI Inference Offloading for UAVs via Distributed Auctions in Dynamic Edge Environments
venue: Journal of Circuits, Systems and Computers
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Autonomous UAVs generate inference tasks and ground edge servers execute eligible offloaded tasks. A distributed auction coordinates UAV bids and server resource offers. [pp. 5–6, §3.1 and Fig. 1; p. 9, §4, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Simulated ResNet-18 image classification tasks use random draws from CIFAR-10 test images, with task input, output and computation sizes specified in the simulator configuration. [p. 19, §6.1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: The task-to-server decision is binary with at most one server per task. Local or deferred operation is described as a fallback. No split by model layer appears in the evaluated assignment variable. [pp. 5–6, §3.1; pp. 9–10, §4.1; p. 11, §4.2, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Discrete-time simulator with modeled ground servers, moving UAVs and an image-classification workload. The paper reports no hardware or live-flight trial in §6. [pp. 19–22, §6.1–6.4, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The design estimates remaining connection time and describes retry, buffering or simplified local operation. A system-level task-success test varies simulated UAV speed and does not isolate retry or fallback. [pp. 9–10, §4.1; pp. 21–22, §6.3 and Fig. 4, PARTIAL]

title: Adaptive model switching of collaborative inference for multi-CNN streams in UAV swarm
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Heterogeneous UAV swarm comprising task UAVs S={S_1,...,S_a} (3 or 4 task UAVs in Fig. 5) and relay UAVs W={W_1,...,W_b} (6 relay UAVs in Fig. 5; 3-7 UAVs per link in Fig. 6c) forming dedicated multi-hop transmission links to a ground station. [PDF p. 3, Section 3, p. 3, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Complex model VGG16 and lightweight model AlexNet evaluated with top-5 accuracy for target tracking/recognition across multiple concurrent CNN streams. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1, p. 8, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED] | The flight trajectories cite Mid-Air. The simulation setup specifies top-5 accuracy but gives no named image dataset for this metric. [PDF p. 2, Section 1 and Section 3, pp. 2-3, inference_model_task_and_dataset:2, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Each stream switches between onboard lightweight model inference and partitioned complex model inference across relay UAVs. [PDF p. 3, Section 3 System model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Trace-driven simulation using Mid-Air UAV trajectory traces and embedded hardware specs (Table 1); specific simulator software name is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1, p. 8, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: UAV swarm follows a predetermined flight trajectory with minor-scale mobility and stable relative positions. [PDF p. 3, Section 3 System model, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: Elastic Collaborative Edge Intelligence for UAV Swarm: Architecture, Challenges, and Opportunities
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: The OODA-loop device–device architecture is tested on four UAV nodes. UAV #1 plans and participates in inference with UAVs #2–#4. [PDF p. 5, Experiment Setup, p. 5, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Faster R-CNN object detection on a video stream (full DNN stored in advance on each UAV); specific video dataset name is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 5, Experiment Setup, p. 5, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: The architecture allocates portions of a pre-stored DNN to selected UAVs. It replans the unfinished portion when a selected UAV becomes unavailable. [PDF p. 4, Architecture Overview, p. 4, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: 4-UAV hardware prototype testbed with one NVIDIA Jetson Nano on UAV#1, one NVIDIA Jetson TX2, and two Jetson Nanos on UAV#2-UAV#4 with airborne communication modules. [PDF p. 5, Section EXPERIMENT SETUP, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Handles UAV unavailability by updating the partition strategy for remaining unfinished parts across available UAVs and recovers speed when the failed node reconnects. [PDF p. 6, Section EFFECT OF UAV UNAVAILABILITY, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: A cognitive synergetic hierarchical framework for UAV swarm combat via speculative inference and role-decoupled reinforcement learning
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: The simulated system uses a hierarchical Brain–Torso architecture, relative pose graph and sequential intention propagation for heterogeneous roles. The main scenarios are 1v1, 2v2 and 6v6; a separate scalability comparison uses 2v2, 4v4, 6v6 and 8v8. [PDF p. 11, Section 5.1.2 and Table 2, pp. 11-12, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The strategic inference experiment uses a workstation-based DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B verifier (AWQ 4-bit) and Jetson-based DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B draft model (INT4). The tactical controller uses a 3×256 actor and two-layer, four-head GAT critic. The modeled strategic and controller frequencies are 5 Hz and 50 Hz. [PDF p. 11, Section 5.1.1 and Table 3, pp. 11, 13, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Decouples a 5 Hz strategic reasoning layer (70B target model at base station and 7B distilled draft model on edge via speculative decoding) from a 50 Hz execution layer via a Zero-Order Hold buffer. [PDF p. 5, Section 4.1 Cognitive synergetic hierarchical architecture, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The simulation uses JSBSim nonlinear six-DOF dynamics and the reported Python C-API wrapper, PyTorch 2.1/CUDA 12.1 and Ubuntu 22.04. The hardware described in §5.1.1 includes two RTX 3090 GPUs and a Jetson AGX Orin. [PDF p. 11, Section 5.1.1 and Table 3, pp. 11, 13, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Evaluated under high delay/jitter (200 +/- 50 ms), Markov flapping links (2 s outage / 5 s in), AWGN (BER 10^-3), and up to 30% packet loss; includes ZOH buffer and Cognitive Fallback to Autonomous-Edge 7B/MAPPO mode on cloud disconnect. [PDF p. 16, Section 5.3.3 and Table 9, pp. 16-17, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: Joint optimization of data sensing and computing in the air–ground collaborative inference framework: A multi-agent hybrid-action DRL approach
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Multiple camera-equipped UAVs survey points of interest. UAVs carry compressed DNNs, while ground edge servers provide uncompressed inference. [pp. 3–4, §3 and Fig. 2, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The analytic workload models temporally correlated multi-frame recognition, with an accuracy function of sampled frame count and a compressed-model penalty. The setup uses 1080 × 1080 frames and allowed frame counts from 5 to 20 with gaps above 13. It reports no real-video experiment. [pp. 5–6, §§3.3–3.4; p. 8, §5.1; p. 12, §6, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Each UAV executes the whole sampled task locally or sends it to one ground edge server. The formulation preserves temporal correlation across sampled frames. [p. 5, §3.3 and Eq. (19); p. 12, §6, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The analytical workload and channel run as simulations on an Ubuntu server. Baseline runs use a scenario with three UAVs, two fixed servers and fifty points of interest. Separate tests vary swarm size. [pp. 8–9, §5.1; p. 11, §5.2.5, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The model varies 3D trajectories and uses a minimum UAV separation. The discussion explicitly omits congestion-related loss and changing locations of mobile points of interest. The evaluated framework does not verify service recovery after node dropout. [p. 4, §3.1.1; pp. 9–11, Table 2 and §5.2; p. 12, §6, PARTIAL]

title: Multi-Agent Meta Reinforcement Learning for Reliable and Low-Latency Distributed Inference in Resource-Constrained UAV Swarms
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Ad hoc wireless UAV swarm collecting IIoT image requests from ground devices and collaboratively executing sequential CNN layers without remote servers. [PDF p. 4, Section III-A UAV SWARM ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATION, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Evaluates image classification using two CNN architectures: 5-layer LeNet and 8-layer AlexNet on 32x32x3 RGB images. [PDF p. 10, Section VI-A SIMULATIONS SETUP, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Each UAV stores a replica of the trained CNN and executes assigned consecutive layers, forwarding intermediate outputs to the next UAV. [PDF p. 4, Section III-A UAV SWARM ARCHITECTURE AND OPERATION, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Custom simulation in Python 3.7.16 with TensorFlow 1.13.1 on Windows (Intel Core i7 / Xeon CPU 2.2 GHz, 4 cores, 16 GB RAM). [PDF p. 10, Section VI, p. 10, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Models dynamic UAV joining/leaving during learning (Fig. 7) and delegates tasks to another UAV while energy-depleted UAVs return to the central station. [PDF p. 6, Section IV Problem Formulation (Constraint C9), mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: LE-MHAPPO-Enhanced DNN Task Partitioning in Energy-Harvesting Heterogeneous UAV Swarms
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Heterogeneous solar-energy-harvesting UAV swarm in a 500 m x 500 m area at fixed altitude H, consisting of I=5 task-receiving UAVs (RUAVs) and J=2 GPU-equipped server UAVs (SUAVs). [PDF p. 5, Section II and Section IV, pp. 2, 5, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: ResNet-18 for image recognition partitioned into P_i=5 blocks (Table I gives local/server cycles and intermediate bits); specific image dataset is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 5, Section IV and Table I, p. 5, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Single split point c_i(T_n) in {0..P_i} partitions the DNN into a local front part on RUAV_i and an offloaded tail part on SUAV_{o_i(T_n)}. [PDF p. 2, Section II-A Task Reception and DNN Partition Inference Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Custom simulation over N=3000 test time slots averaged across 5 randomly generated flight/task-arrival trajectories (10 seeds for convergence); simulator software is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 5, Section IV, p. 5, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The motion model has velocity and acceleration constraints and repulsive collision avoidance. The long-timescale energy model represents separate local-computation and offloading pauses when the relevant energy counter reaches zero. [PDF p. 2, Section II-B Energy Harvesting Model, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: End-to-End Latency Optimization for Resilient Distributed Convolutional Neural Network Inference in Resource-Constrained Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Swarms
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Wireless ad hoc swarm of N UAVs communicating via U2U links and transmitting final inference outputs to a ground device via a U2G link. [PDF p. 3, Section 2 System Model, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Evaluates three CNNs: 8-layer AlexNet and 16-layer VGG16 (trained on ILSVRC 2014) and 20-layer YOLO (trained on PASCAL VOC 2007). [PDF p. 9, Section 5.1 Simulation Settings and Table 1, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Each UAV holds a copy of the trained CNN and executes layers dynamically assigned by DRL-RLD based on memory, compute, position, and operability. [PDF p. 4, Section 2 System Model, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Evaluation uses simulation; Fig. 3 plots training reward through episode 1000. The inspected methods and experimental setup do not identify simulation software or host hardware. [PDF p. 9, Section 5.1, p. 9, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Tracks an inoperable state parameter per UAV (0 to 2 inoperable UAVs per episode) and dynamically reallocates layers across remaining operational UAVs. [PDF p. 4, Section 2 System Model, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: Orion: A Collaborative Edge Inference Framework for Large Language Models Processing Multi-Sensor Data in UAV Swarms
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Pure-edge heterogeneous UAV pipeline (3x AGX Orin 16 GB, 1x Orin NX 32 GB) that strictly prohibits cloud offloading. [PDF p. 7, Section 3.1.1 System Model and Problem Formulation, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Llama-2 (7B, 13B, 70B in FP16) with causal KV cache processing simulated textual multi-modal UAV sensor logs (16, 32, 64, 128 tokens) for swarm coordination. [PDF p. 15, Section 4.1 and Table 1, pp. 15-16, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Combines state-compressed DP layer-to-device partitioning (Algorithm 1) with Min-Max DP adaptive non-uniform sequence chunking (Algorithm 2) and first-token predictive decoding. [PDF p. 6, Section 3 Proposed Solution: The Orion Framework, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Custom simulation framework implemented in Python 3.13.5 modeling hardware profiles, network bandwidth/jitter, and LLM prefill/decode execution. [PDF p. 14, Section 4.1, p. 14, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Evaluates robustness under +/-20% inter-UAV bandwidth fluctuation and Monte Carlo multiplicative Gaussian computation (10%/30%) and communication (20%/30%) noise. [PDF p. 21, Section 4.8 Robustness Analysis Under Environmental Uncertainty, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: CIDER: Collaborative Inference with Distilled Early-Exit Routing for Multi-UAV Edge Networks
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Assistant UAVs compute branches of a multi-exit student model and transmit selected intermediate features. A master forms the final prediction from its own representation and the received features. [pp. 4–5, §III.A–C, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification with Wide Residual Network teachers and lighter multi-exit students. The experiment uses classification benchmarks in place of aerial imagery. [pp. 8–9, §IV.A and Table I; p. 13, §IV.E, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: The offline alignment method assigns ranked teacher feature channels to student branches using device-capacity allocation and deterministic overlap. The master can select different exit depths for different assistants. [pp. 4–5, §III.C; pp. 6–8, §III.D and Algorithm 1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Hardware profiles feed a simulation with saved channel traces and separate validation/test roles. It is a profiled simulation of routing, with no full distributed on-device deployment reported. [pp. 8–10, §IV.A–B and Tables I–III; p. 13, §IV.E, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Time-varying link rates, bandwidth sweeps and assistant waiting are represented. The reported setup does not establish live mobility, a node-failure test or restart performance. [pp. 8–9, §IV.A; p. 11, §IV.C; p. 13, §IV.E, PARTIAL]

title: Distributed split computing using diffusive metrics for UAV swarms
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Swarm nodes exchange local capacity metrics with one-hop neighbors; repeated exchanges propagate workload information beyond one hop. There is no global scheduler in the proposed method. [pp. 3–5, §§1 and 3, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The simulator processes a modeled layered inference graph with two intermediate exits. The evaluation identifies an application example, with no named input dataset or specified neural-network implementation. [pp. 4 and 8, §3 and Table 2, PARTIAL]
partition_and_assignment: A node can forward raw inputs or already computed intermediate state to a neighbor, choosing a layer exit depth with respect to load. The method bounds redundant reconsideration. [pp. 2 and 5–8, Fig. 2 and §4, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The evaluation is software simulation with stochastic arrivals, mobility and heterogeneous nodes. It describes repeated independent runs, with no physical UAV test in the evaluation. [p. 8, §5 and Table 2, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Circular UAV trajectories and mostly line-of-sight connections drive modeled neighbor changes. Constraint and queue behavior mitigates redistribution loops. Physical node failure and recovery are not evaluated in the inspected simulation. [pp. 6 and 8, §§4 and 5, PARTIAL]

title: Edge-Cloud Collaborative Model Inference for Aerial Networks with Distributionally Diverse Data
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: Multiple aerial edge nodes independently extract features and collaborate with one ground/cloud server via a modeled radio access network. [pp. 2–3, §II.A and Fig. 1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: CIFAR-10 test images are augmented to synthesize non-identical data across UAVs. ResNet-18/34 act as edge backbones and ResNet-101/152 act as cloud backbones. [p. 5, §IV.A, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Cloud processing of uploaded features estimates confidence, then a per-UAV threshold selects cases requiring an additional quantized raw upload. [pp. 2–3, §II.A and Fig. 1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The edge–cloud experiment is simulated using synthesized data distributions. The cloud processing hardware is identified; there is no demonstrated flight test in this experiment. [p. 5, §IV.A, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: No UAV trajectory, outage or recovery evaluation is reported in the configuration or results. Spectral efficiency differences do not establish mobility validation. [pp. 2 and 5–6, §§II.A and IV, NOT_REPORTED]

title: LLHR: Low Latency and High Reliability CNN Distributed Inference for Resource-Constrained UAV Swarms
venue: 2023 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (WCNC)
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: UAV cameras generate image classification requests; same-altitude UAVs cooperate over a wireless ad hoc network. The inference path is intra-swarm.
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Surveillance image classification using LeNet and AlexNet. The evaluated image dataset is not named in §IV.
partition_and_assignment: Discrete assignment of each CNN layer to one UAV, with memory and compute bounds and modeled delegation on insufficient capacity.
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Simulation with synthetic surveillance grid and Raspberry Pi B+ device profiles. Figures 2–5 show average latency and minimum radio transmit power; Fig. 5 uses static-path and random-movement baselines.
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The link model is line-of-sight and distance dependent; position choice respects modeled separation. The minimum transmission-rate constraint represents link reliability. No outage, link loss or failure/recovery trial is reported in §IV.

title: Distributed inference in IoT-based aerial network of UAVs
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: 802.11s mesh swarm of N UAVs comprising a center UAV (gateway/scheduler, non-computing), requesting UAVs, and worker UAVs. [PDF p. 3, Section 3.1.1 UAV swarm, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The simulated search-and-rescue scenario includes concurrent AlexNet and VGG19 requests for object/person detection. The evaluation uses modeled inference profiles; the data availability statement says no data was used. [PDF p. 6, Section 4.1 and Data availability, pp. 6, 9, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Virtualizes worker UAV compute and deploys DNN partitions as containers managed by a per-UAV Container Manager using a heuristic placement algorithm. [PDF p. 3, Section 3.1.2 Deployment process, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Python implementation of Algorithm 1 and network/energy simulation; specific simulator package or host hardware is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 6, Section 3.6, p. 6, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: Reference Point Group (RPG) 2-D mobility at fixed altitude z with 802.11s contention packet drop rate (PDR) and heterogeneous battery levels (halving battery on half of UAVs); node failure/recovery is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 4, Section 3.3 and 4.2, pp. 4, 7, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: A hybrid fast inference approach with distributed neural networks for edge computing enabled UAV swarm
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: 12 drone terminals connected via wireless links to 4 aerial computing centers (edge servers) interconnected in a line topology via laser transmission. [PDF p. 5, Section 3.4 Problem formulation and Section 5 (Page 8), uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Branchy ResNet image classification model (32 total layers) trained and tested on CIFAR-10 (50,000 train, 10,000 test 32x32 RGB images). [PDF p. 5, Section 3.3 Model training, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Deploys a 10-layer head network with bottleneck early-exit on drones and full 32-layer model on aerial servers, supporting local exit, split upload, or direct offload. [PDF p. 5, Section 3.3 Model training, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: DNN built and trained in PyTorch; simulation averaged over 5,000 cycles per experiment; host hardware is NOT_REPORTED. [PDF p. 8, Section 5, p. 8, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: UAV mobility, dynamic topology changes, and node/link failure recovery are not modeled in the simulation (explicitly noted as future work in Section 6). [PDF p. 11, Section 6, p. 11, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, NOT_REPORTED]

title: Aeroagrinet: Swarm-Enabled Flying Edge Framework for Real-Time Agricultural Intelligence
venue: 2025 International Conference on Engineering Innovations and Technologies (ICoEIT)
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: A layered flying-edge system uses coordinated UAVs with onboard inference, ground sensor connections and optional cloud synchronization. [pp. 2–3, §II and Figs. 2–3, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The paper describes crop-pest detection, vegetation and soil monitoring, and yield prediction. It reports lightweight CNN edge benchmarking, but does not identify specific input datasets for those benchmarks. [pp. 4–5, §§IV and V.J, PARTIAL]
partition_and_assignment: Onboard inference tasks are assigned or reassigned across drones. The cited design is task-level allocation with local inference; no layer-level split is described in the relevant sections. [pp. 2–3, §§II.B and III.B, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The authors describe simulation with NS-3, ROS, Gazebo and MATLAB UAV Toolbox and a separate author-reported DJI/Raspberry Pi/Coral field prototype. [p. 4, §V.E, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The design describes self-healing connectivity and redundant reassignment. Dropout and packet-loss results are reported, with no explicit link assigning the individual dropout comparison to the hardware field prototype. [pp. 3 and 5–6, §§II.D, III.B, V.F and V.K, PARTIAL]

title: A DRL-Assisted Decentralized Framework for UAV Swarm Collaborative Inference
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: The simulated swarm is decentralized, with two UAVs collaborating per inference. The task pipeline is distinct from swarm population; Table IV gives the default and Table X varies it. [pp. 5–6, 10–11 and 15, §III.E and Tables IV and X, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The workload uses image minibatches and profiled model configurations, including four networks in Table V and an additional transfer-analysis model. Named source image data are not reported in the setup. [pp. 5, 10, 13 and 14–15, §III.D, §V.A and Table V, PARTIAL]
partition_and_assignment: Each task can pair its source with a selected neighbor and split a DNN at a candidate layer. The mini-batch pipeline overlaps communication and processing, with a local option. [pp. 5–8, §§III.D–E and IV, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: A custom Gymnasium simulator and a PyTorch/Stable-Baselines3 learner evaluate a set of common-seed episodes. Named hardware characteristics inform simulated compute profiles. [pp. 10–11, §V.A–C and Table IV, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The simulator models changing neighbors and link interruptions. The design includes assignment or local fallback handling. This is software evaluation rather than field-validated recovery. [pp. 3–4 and 11–12, §III.A, §III.C and §V.E–G, OBSERVED]

title: Multi-UAV cooperative inference for IoVs: Dynamic partitioning and caching optimization
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: 5-UAV swarm in a 1000 m x 1000 m area with 1 core UAV (global state collection and PPO-DMCP scheduling) and 4 computing UAVs executing DNN partitions. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1 Experimental environment and parameter settings, uav_architecture_role_and_topology:1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: Models DNNs as 10-macro-block sequences and evaluates generalization across ResNet50, MobileNetV3, and BERT; focuses on latency rather than accuracy. [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1 Experimental environment and parameter settings, inference_model_task_and_dataset:1, OBSERVED]
partition_and_assignment: Selects N-1 ordered split points across L macro-blocks for pipeline parallelism, paired with a priority-aware cache replacement policy (weighting access frequency and loading latency) for 200 MB per-UAV caches. [PDF p. 4, Section 3.3 and 3.4, pp. 4-5, partition_and_assignment:1, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: Simulated on a Windows 11 (64-bit) server with 12th Gen Intel Core i5-12600KF, 32 GB RAM, and NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 GPU; 20,000 PPO episodes (20 steps/episode). [PDF p. 8, Section 5.1, p. 8, evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_and_traces:1, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The model controls planar displacement with a 5 m minimum separation. A backup controller is described as a possible failover for the core UAV. The reported experiments do not include a failover evaluation. [PDF p. 8, Section 3.1 and 4.5, pp. 4, 8, mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_and_recovery:1, OBSERVED]

title: Robust Group Target Awareness Inference in Multi-UAV-Enabled ISCC Networks Based on Split Deep Reinforcement Learning
uav_architecture_role_and_topology: A multi-UAV system coordinates compute among airborne nodes and distributes inference within the airborne group. [pp. 3–4, §III and Fig. 1, OBSERVED]
inference_model_task_and_dataset: The evaluation uses a layered neural network and software workload profiles. No underlying input dataset is identified in the inspected setup. [p. 10, §V and Table II, PARTIAL]
partition_and_assignment: The architecture allocates sequential portions of a split neural workload across participating UAVs. [p. 4, §III.A and Fig. 2, OBSERVED]
evaluation_platform_simulator_hardware_a: The authors report Python/PyTorch numerical simulation with a GPU for the study configuration. The evaluation is not a live or hardware testbed study. [p. 10, §V and Table II, OBSERVED]
mobility_channel_intermittency_failure_a: The software evaluation varies node participation and inspects the ability to continue inference after node losses. Hardware recovery is not demonstrated. [pp. 10–13, §V, OBSERVED]

title: Joint Semantic Compression and Resource Allocation for Multi-UAV Networks: A Knowledge-Guided Reinforcement Learning Approach
